correctness.rationale: Zero a_i requires W_B−y_i>=2, zero b_i requires W_A−x_i>=2: these are exact open-neighborhood sums. For total weight <=2 at n=3 or <=3 at n>=4, one side has sum <=1 and forces every vertex of the opposite side positive, contradicting the target weight. At weight 3 (n=3) only the two all-one-side functions work. At weight 4 (n>=4), any side weight <=1 forces a full opposite side, possible only for n=4 with two all-one-side functions. Otherwise both sides have weight two. Every positive label on one side must be at a positive matched index on the opposite side since a zero excludes exactly its matched opposite; supports coincide, and weight-two support has size one with each label 2 or size two with four labels 1. Hence n+binom(n,2), plus two when n=4. Independently enumerated every labeling of total weight <=4 for n=3..10; minima counts 2,12,15,21,28,36,45,55 and minima weights 3,4,...,4. The infinite result comes from the support argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: On the natural crown graph, deleting one perfect matching changes domination constraints in a precisely measurable way; the theorem classifies every minimum Italian labeling, not just gamma=4. It proves an integer transition at n=4 and exact n+binom(n,2) optimizer counts after n=5, potentially useful for extremal enumeration/algorithm tests. This is an exact structural family classification beyond a textbook bound.

final_claim: For crown Cr_n and Italian/Roman-{2} domination, n=3 has gamma=3 and exactly two all-one-side minima; n=4 has gamma=4 and exactly 12 minima; for n>=5 gamma=4 and minima are exactly n aligned dual-2 deleted-pair supports and binom(n,2) aligned four-unit 1-labelled two-pair supports, giving binom(n+1,2) minima.
limitations: Only Italian/Roman-{2} (not perfect, secure or total) domination on crowns n>=3.
Unindexed earlier same-object theorem remains possible.
